question: L.i) = Why is Swing preferred over AWT?
answerMd:
### AWT vs. Swing in Java

| Comparison Parameter | Abstract Window Toolkit (AWT) | Swing (JFC) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Component Weight** | **Heavyweight:** Relies on native OS GUI peers. | **Lightweight:** Written 100% in pure Java. |
| **Look and Feel** | **Platform-dependent:** Looks different on Windows vs Linux. | **Pluggable Look-and-Feel (PLAF):** Uniform or customizable. |
| **Component Richness**| Basic controls (Button, Label, Checkbox). | Rich set: JTable, JTree, JTabbedPane, JColorChooser. |
| **Component Prefix** | None (`Button`, `Frame`, `Label`). | Prefixed with `J` (`JButton`, `JFrame`, `JLabel`). |
| **Architecture** | Simple procedural/event wrapper. | Adheres to **Model-View-Controller (MVC)** design. |

$$\therefore \text{Swing components are 100% pure Java lightweight controls providing cross-platform visual consistency.}$$
